### problem_chain

- Root: calibration goodwill (warranty_ext_calibration_goodwill, trigger on_request) — the customer asks "whether anything can be done about that inspection fee" ("That is the only thing you are calling about").
- Walk from the root rule: its prerequisite sentence "Calibration goodwill is figured only after the calibration diagnostic charge owed on the not-covered calibration finding stands on the coverage's account." At `frozen_time` the coverage's money history (`initial_state.warranty_ledger`) is empty — no charge stands on concern 2. The policy whose own rule posts "one calibration diagnostic charge for that concern" is warranty_ext_calibration_diagnostic_charge; its rule carries no prerequisite sentence (and `prerequisite: []`). Its write is `accept_calibration_diagnostic_charge_d9578b72`, owner=user.
- Derived tree: nodes {goodwill (agent), calibration charge (user)}; edge goodwill <- charge, `value_input` (the charge amount is the base the goodwill share acts on). n = 1 prerequisite problem, value_input edges = 1 ≥ max(0,1). Isomorphic to the declared E1.
- Topological order: calibration charge -> calibration goodwill.
- Edge false at opening: `warranty_ledger` has 0 rows in the masked `initial_state`.
- Load-bearing run: skipping the charge write and evaluating the goodwill on the opening world gives 16.20 (charge_amount 0.00; 0 × 0.10 + 13.50 = 13.50, × 1.2 = 16.20) instead of 33.47; and the waiver would have no charge entry to name. Bears weight.
- Customer's own write in the tree: the charge acceptance (owner=user), handed over at the agent's direction (persona: "When the agent hands you the step to accept the charge, you accept it exactly as the agent describes it").
- Parallel edges: none.
- No wait: acceptance is immediate.
- Tools do not judge: `accept_calibration_diagnostic_charge_d9578b72` and `grant_calibration_goodwill_f9a2e5bf` each do one `ctx.create` with caller values; no read of the ledger, no refusal (task_tools.py lines 19–49, 120–150).

Persona closes after the goodwill is applied ("Once the agent tells you how much of the fee they can take off and that the reduction has been applied, you thank them ... and end the call").

## findings

**T0-1 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED: the alignment tier rests on adas rows the adas charter forbids.**
- Symptom: the calibration alignment fee is charged at the "out of specification and corrected" tier (29.95) because the customer's most recent alignment check is an out_of_spec check on an order that was prechecked, calibrated and completed with no later in-spec check.
- Root cause: the seeded adas history of orders `ec22bf5a…` and `1f4b3712…` omits the re-check the adas charter requires before a precheck, so the latest check on file is a corrected out_of_spec check.
- Evidence: `blueprint/products/adas.yaml` adas_evt_precheck rule: "Where alignment_required is true, the most recent alignment check on the order is in_spec and was made no more than the tier's alignment check validity days before the precheck. ... An out_of_spec check must be corrected and checked again"; eligibility `alignment_in_spec_recent` (same condition); Multi-System Calibration `alignment_required: true`. Seed: `initial_state.adas_orders.ec22bf5a-4314-4f41-b26a-5c4bb084efa9` (`status: completed`, `precheck_date: 2026-07-16`) whose only alignment check is `initial_state.adas_events.daa77808-5477-4bf3-8bee-759dd50b8e0d` (2026-07-16, `out_of_spec`, `alignment_corrected: true`, `check_number: 1`); same pattern on `1f4b3712…` (`b9eecbc7…` 2026-01-20 out_of_spec, precheck 2026-01-20, completed). Secondary contradictions on `1f4b3712…` not read by any factor: `retry_requires_new_precheck: true` (Multi-System) but no alignment check precedes the 2026-01-22 retry; the correction posted `alignment_correction` 129.95 with no `alignment_check` charge although the rule says "on a customer-pay order the check posts an alignment_check charge and a correction an alignment_correction charge".
- Demonstrated consequence: replay with the charter-required in-spec re-check on `ec22bf5a…` (check_number 2, dated after the correction) — the rule's "most recent four-wheel alignment check recorded on the customer's calibration orders" is in_spec, the alignment fee falls to the fall-through (0), the charge is 113.95 instead of 143.90 and the goodwill 29.87 instead of 33.47 (`/tmp/audit_0052_wrd/t0.py`). The tier the task scores is therefore one an adas history obeying its own charter cannot produce for this customer; the task tests the reading of a world that the adas desk's own rules say cannot exist.
- Affected: `tasks/warranty_rework_desk/tasks/0.json` `initial_state.adas_events` (orders ec22bf5a…, 1f4b3712…) and `initial_state.adas_ledger` (1f4b3712… charges); `computations[0]` (expected 143.9, factor_trace for calibration_alignment_fee) and, through charge_amount, `computations[1]` (33.47); evaluation_criteria step 12 and step 14 amount_usd.
- Relation to previous revisions: first audit revision of this difficulty.

Observations:
- T0-O1 (cites `_difficulty.md` F-1): the "network reworks" rule/compute split does not reach this coverage (CWW sublet distance 0); no consequence here.
- T0-O2 calibration_alignment_fee is labelled multi-source in `computations[0].factor_trace` and the design card although both of its tier conditions are fields of one adas_events row; not a world fact and the task's multi-source floor is met by calibration_low_use_allowance.
- T0-O3 The persona's conditional line "If the agent explains that the inspection charge has to be on your account first and asks whether you agree to it" is passive (triggered only by the agent's explanation) and does not name a prerequisite unprompted; no short-circuit.
- T0-O4 O-14 of `_difficulty.md` (history surcharge on the network's own failed attempt) applies here: the 20.00 history fee rests on the network's failed dynamic attempt `a51dee1c…`.
